subject: Request: Clarify K8s logging carve-out + bridge letter scope for SOC2 audit
messages:
From: audit@acmecorp.com
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2 Type II — clarification on logging subservice/carve-out and bridge letter

Hi Tessa,

We are kicking off the SOC 2 Type II fieldwork for Acme Financial and have a few clarifying asks related to your hosted offering's managed logging pipeline. Specifically: 1) We need confirmation whether Redwood is carving out any managed logging agent/service that is operated by LogStream (your logging subprocessor). If so, we need the scope of that carve-out documented. 2) If Redwood is relying on LogStream's SOC/attestation for any portion of the control environment (ingest, parsing, transient KV storage), please confirm and provide either LogStream's SOC 2 report for the audit period (Jan 1 2026–Dec 31 2026) or a bridge letter from LogStream that covers the overlapping audit period and the specific control areas. 3) Please provide a list of subprocessors related to log ingestion, processing, and long-term storage (S3 buckets or equivalent), even if some are upstream.

We have attached a short questionnaire (acme-soc2-questionnaire-2026.pdf) with the exact artifacts we typically request. If you expect any delays in sharing the vendor attestation/bridge letter, let us know the earliest ETA so we can indicate it to the audit team.

Thanks,
Lina Park
Acme Financial — Security Assurance

--
Acme: compliance@acmecorp.com
From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
To: audit@acmecorp.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — clarification on logging subservice/carve-out and bridge letter

Hi Lina — thanks for the note and for the questionnaire. Looping in Marissa (security/compliance lead) and Ben (sales/legal liaison) to coordinate artifacts and the vendor bridge letter.

Short answers up front: we do not plan to carve out customer-controlled persistent storage for logs (S3 buckets) — customers who opt into Redwood-managed logging may have events routed through LogStream for ingestion/transform, but long-term storage is in our AWS accounts (Redwood-managed S3). That said, LogStream does operate our ingest pipeline (transient processing and parsing) for a subset of customers in the managed logging offering and we do rely on them for certain operational controls (availability and initial parsing).

Next steps from our side:
- Marissa will pull our subprocessor inventory and the LogStream SOC report/bridge letter if available.
- Ben will reach out to LogStream for a narrow bridge letter if they cannot provide a full SOC 2 for the audit period.
- We'll produce an evidence package listing where control ownership sits (ingest vs storage vs retention) and a short architecture diagram showing the handoff boundary.

We expect to have an initial package (inventory + architecture diagram + vendor outreach status) by end of day 22 Dec. Does that timeline work for your auditors?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Compliance Programs (interim)
Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — clarification on logging subservice/carve-out and bridge letter

Tessa — pulling the items now. Quick notes and what I'll attach:

1) Subprocessor inventory (attached: subproc_inventory-2026.csv) — includes LogStream (ingest), CloudStorageCo (S3 hosting for archived logs), and TranscodeOps (parsing helpers).
2) Architecture diagram (attached: k8s-logging-arch-2026-11.pdf) — shows the ingress edge, LogStream-managed parsing layer, then transfer to Redwood-managed S3 with KMS-encrypted buckets.
3) Evidence we can provide from Redwood: network flow logs (VPC flow), KMS key ownership doc, S3 access logs, and retention/eraser runbook references.
4) Vendor attestation status: LogStream has a SOC 2 for their CY2025 period but has not provided a 2026 report yet; they've confirmed they plan to close 2026 Type II in Q1 2027. They offered to provide a bridge letter scoped to "ingest & transient processing" for the 2026 audit period.

Recommendation: request a narrowly scoped bridge letter from LogStream that explicitly lists the control categories they cover (availability, change control for the ingest layer, incident response) and states the audit period coverage. That keeps the scope tight and avoids confusing long-term storage controls which are managed by Redwood.

I will attach the two files mentioned and a short internal mapping matrix that maps each control to ownership (Redwood vs LogStream). ETA: I will send the package by 16:00 PT today.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: vendor-ops@logstream.io
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Bridge letter for overlapping SOC 2 period (2026) — sample template included

Hi LogStream team —

We're supporting an upstream audit request from a customer (Acme Financial) who is asking for LogStream's SOC coverage for the period Jan 1 2026–Dec 31 2026, or a bridge letter that confirms controls for that period. We understand you may not yet have the full 2026 Type II report; a narrowly scoped bridge letter will be sufficient if it:
- Confirms the audit period covered by your prior report (CY2025) and explicitly states which control areas remain the same through Dec 31 2026, or
- Confirms that you maintain controls covering ingest/transient processing for the period Jan 1–Dec 31 2026 and lists the control categories (availability, change mgmt for ingest pipelines, incident response).

Attached is a short sample bridge letter template you can use (we can adapt as needed). Please let us know by COB 23 Dec if you can provide the letter and a point of contact for our auditors to validate.

Forwarded template (short):
[LogStream Letterhead]
To whom it may concern — This letter confirms that LogStream maintained the following control categories for the period Jan 1 2026 through Dec 31 2026: [list]. The design and operation of these controls were consistent with the control environment described in LogStream's SOC 2 report dated 2025-12-31. This letter is provided to support reliance by third parties and is limited to the control categories and period stated here.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
To: audit@acmecorp.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — clarification on logging subservice/carve-out and bridge letter

Hi Lina — quick update from Redwood:

- Attached items (to follow in separate secure share): subprocessor inventory (subproc_inventory-2026.csv), logging architecture (k8s-logging-arch-2026-11.pdf), and a mapping of controls to ownership (Redwood vs LogStream).
- LogStream has committed to providing a scoped bridge letter that covers ingest/transient processing for the 2026 period. Ben has reached out and we expect a response by 23 Dec COB.
- We confirm that persistent log storage (long-term S3 archival) is Redwood-managed and not carved out to LogStream. Controls for storage, retention, and encryption are in Redwood's scope.

If your auditors need a narrow statement that delineates each control's owner (e.g., "Redwood: data-at-rest encryption; LogStream: ingest availability"), we can provide that matrix. Please advise if the audit team needs the bridge letter to include specific control IDs or test examples — we can ask LogStream to include brief examples (e.g., sampling of change management tickets for the ingest cluster) but would prefer to keep the bridge letter limited in scope.

Best,
Tessa
[Attachments referenced across the thread: acme-soc2-questionnaire-2026.pdf (requested), subproc_inventory-2026.csv (inventory stub), k8s-logging-arch-2026-11.pdf (architecture diagram stub), logstream-bridge-letter-template.docx (sample template - stub)]
